Below is a pair of *SEARCH/REPLACE* patches that tighten the single‐line comment part so that it stops at the end of its own line instead of consuming everything to EOF. We replace `(?:--|\/\/|#).*` with `(?:--|\/\/|#)[^\r\n]*` in both the non‐minified and minified SQL language definitions.

```javascript
### components/prism-sql.js
<<<<<<< SEARCH
    'comment': {
        pattern: /(^|[^\\])(?:\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\/|(?:--|\/\/|#).*)/,
        lookbehind: true
    },
=======
    'comment': {
        pattern: /(^|[^\\])(?:\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\/|(?:--|\/\/|#)[^\r\n]*)/,
        lookbehind: true
    },
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

```javascript
### components/prism-sql.min.js
<<<<<<< SEARCH
comment:{pattern:/(^|[^\\])(?:\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\/|(?:--|\/\/|#).*)/,lookbehind:!0},
=======
comment:{pattern:/(^|[^\\])(?:\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\/|(?:--|\/\/|#)[^\r\n]*)/,lookbehind:!0},
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

Explanation of the change:

- We switch from `.*` (which, in Prism’s internal engine, can cross line breaks) to a more precise `[^\r\n]*`, ensuring that `--`, `//` or `#` comments consume only until the end of that line. This restores correct syntax highlighting for subsequent SQL statements.
